policies.name: Low-Sodium Diet (2,000 mg/day)
policies.description: Common hospital '2 g sodium' diet. Daily cap follows the WHO adult recommendation; per-meal caps are example institutional rules.

sources.label: WHO adult guideline: sodium intake < 2 g/day (< 5 g salt/day)

rules.description: Total daily sodium must not exceed 2,000 mg.
Spread sodium across the day: no main meal above 800 mg.
No snack above 400 mg sodium.
Avoid cured meats, instant noodles, regular canned soups and salty condiments.

policies.name: Strict Low-Sodium Diet (1,500 mg/day)
policies.description: Extends the 2 g diet with the stricter AHA ideal limit.

sources.label: AHA: ideal limit 1,500 mg sodium/day for most adults

rules.description: Total daily sodium must not exceed 1,500 mg.

policies.name: Diabetic Consistent-Carbohydrate Diet
policies.description: Typical institutional consistent-carbohydrate (CCHO) meal pattern for adults with diabetes, plus general Dietary Guidelines limits. ADA recommends individualised targets, so every number here is configurable.

sources.label: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes - Nutrition therapy (individualised, consistent carbohydrate intake)
Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025 (sodium, saturated fat, added sugars, fiber)

rules.description: Main meals must not exceed 60 g carbohydrate.
Main meals should provide at least 45 g carbohydrate to match medication or insulin.
Snacks should stay at or below 30 g carbohydrate.
Carbohydrate should be similar across main meals (within 15 g).
Sugar-sweetened beverages are not allowed.
Avoid cakes, pastries and other concentrated sweets.
Added sugars should supply less than 10% of daily energy.
rules.source: Dietary Guidelines for Americans; WHO free-sugars guideline

rules.description: Saturated fat should supply less than 10% of daily energy.
Provide at least 14 g fiber per 1,000 kcal.
Daily sodium should stay below 2,300 mg.
Lunch and dinner should include a non-starchy vegetable.
Plan at least three main meals so carbohydrate is spread evenly.

policies.name: Diabetic + Low-Sodium Diet
policies.description: Common combined hospital order. Later 'extends' entries override earlier ones, so the 2 g sodium rule replaces the 2,300 mg guideline.

policies.name: Philippine National Guidelines (NGF 2012 + Pinggang Pinoy)
policies.description: The Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos messages are qualitative (no numeric limits), so they are codified as per-meal plate-composition checks and flag-for-review warnings rather than hard numeric limits.

sources.label: DOST-FNRI Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos (2012 revision): limit salty, sugar-rich, fatty and fried foods; eat more vegetables and fruits; eat fish, lean meat, poultry, eggs, beans or nuts daily
DOST-FNRI Pinggang Pinoy: plate with grain, meat/fish, vegetable and fruit portions; a cup of rice is the main feature of the grain portion

rules.description: Each main meal should include a grain/starch portion (rice, corn, bread, root crop).
Each main meal should include fish, lean meat, poultry, egg, beans or nuts.
Each main meal should include vegetables.
Each main meal should include a fruit.
Reference portion of about 1 cup of cooked rice per main meal (rice foods are defined per cup). Adjustable by the institution.
rules.source: Pinggang Pinoy (a cup of rice in the grain portion)

rules.description: Flag salty foods (bagoong, patis, tuyo, processed meats, instant noodles, chicharon) for review.
Flag sugar-sweetened drinks (soft drinks, powdered juice drinks, 3-in-1 coffee) for review.
Flag sweets and desserts (halo-halo, leche flan, turon, banana cue) for review.
Flag fried foods for review.
rules.source: NGF 2012: limit fatty and fried foods

policies.institution: TEMPLATE - replace with your hospital's own diet manual values
policies.description: Philippine national plate guidance plus a 2,000 mg/day sodium limit (the WHO benchmark that Philippine sodium-reduction advocacy refers to). Not an official policy of any specific hospital.

policies.name: Davao City Hospital - Diabetic Diet (template)
policies.institution: TEMPLATE - replace with your hospital's own diet manual values
policies.description: Philippine national plate guidance plus a consistent-carbohydrate pattern. The Pinggang Pinoy vegetable check replaces the lunch/dinner-only vegetable rule. Not an official policy of any specific hospital.

rules.description: Daily sodium should stay below 2,000 mg (WHO benchmark).
rules.source: WHO: < 2,000 mg sodium (< 5 g salt) per day

policies.name: Davao City Hospital - Diabetic + Low-Sodium Diet (template)
policies.institution: TEMPLATE - replace with your hospital's own diet manual values
policies.description: Combined order: Philippine plate guidance + consistent carbohydrate + 2,000 mg sodium (error level). Later 'extends' entries override earlier ones with the same rule id, so the clinical rules are stricter than the national flag-for-review rules.
